For me it has to be Deus Ex.
What is the most thought provoking game series you've played?

Games like that are rare but perhaps Mafia: The City of Lost Heaven, where the level of story telling was beyond anything I had experienced before that point. Finally a game that tried to tell a story for an adult audience. Like Goodfellas or something. A more recent example would be perhaps DayZ. It really makes you wonder about humanity and whether or not we would tear each other apart in a global crisis. I don't personally really think so, but if we had weapons lying around everywhere, then who knows.

Stanley Parable - Because it just was. What is free will and all that good stuff.

Portal series - For the mind bending gameplay/physics puzzles.

Fallout 3 - For the exploration of a thought experiment in which future tech collides with pre coldwar social ideologies. Bonus points for exploring the complexity of how the power vaccum of a post apocalyptic society might be filled.

GTA IV - Really did a good job of exploring the shades of grey surrounding criminality and the lifestyle it leads to.

Deus Ex - Was an interesting look at the future of Biomedicine and what that will mean for those who can and cannot access said technology.

Thats all that I can think of off the top of my head.

And the Halo series

I'd have to say The Witcher. There are some choices in those games that had me sitting there for a good 5-10 mins, staring at the dialogue options. Even better that there's no clear good/bad, so there's usually unintended consequences to your actions. In most games, it feels like my moral choices are based on, "what ending do I want?" but in the Witcher it's, "what impact do I want to make? how will these characters feel towards me?"

Fallout New Vegas - Makes Fallout 3 feel like it was written by a high-school dropout. ( Fallout 3 is great but New Vegas is that much better imo.)

Alpha Centauri - The tech and secret project quotes will make you stand back and think for awhile, my favourite being this one by Lal's https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iY57ErBkFFE

Bioshock - Atlas Shrugged meets underwater dystopia, don't want to spoiler it for anyone who hasn't played the first one but the narrative is tight and the recorded stories make you question all sorts of moral and ethical stances.
